passage: L1.4: "If a dataset with duplicates is used for the purposes of training and evaluating an ML model," [the rest: the same data could exist in the training set and the test set] (Results, 'Toward a solution: A taxonomy of data leakage', PMC10499856; sentence cut by the fetch tool).
faulty: 1-nearest-neighbour regression (Euclidean distance on X standardised with the training mean and sd) under 5-fold cross-validation (fold = i mod 5) on all 1200 records as given; Pearson correlation between the pooled held-out predictions and y >= 0.30.
fixed: Records whose standardised X rows lie closer than 0.1 times the median pairwise distance are linked (single linkage, connected components); every component is placed whole into one fold (component id mod 5 after ordering by first member); the same 5-fold evaluation; Pearson correlation >= 0.30.
estimand: Faulty: correlation on held-out records many of which have a near-identical record among the fitting records. Fixed: correlation for new compounds that have no near-identical record among those used to fit.
model_family: 1-nearest-neighbour regression, Euclidean distance on standardised descriptors; numpy-only, and it returns the response of a near-identical record. Same model as B2A-06 but with near-copies (not exact), correlation, and a larger sample.
sizes_note: Source states none. 1200 x 20 = 24,000 values; a 1200 x 1200 distance matrix is built once and per fold (seconds). Dependence on sample size or duplicate share: not stated. With one neighbour and a share f of records that have a near copy, the correlation under no effect is about f, so a threshold of 0.30 corresponds to about 30% such records.
exploited_structure: Near-identical records (same entity measured or entered more than once with slight differences) in different parts of the data, so a held-out record has a near copy, with nearly the same response, among the fitting records.

def stat(d):
    X = np.asarray(d["X"], dtype=float)
    X = (X - X.mean(axis=0)) / (X.std(axis=0) + 1e-12)
    sq = (X ** 2).sum(axis=1)
    D = np.sqrt(np.maximum(sq[:, None] + sq[None, :] - 2.0 * (X @ X.T), 0.0))
    n = D.shape[0]
    med = np.median(D[~np.eye(n, dtype=bool)])
    np.fill_diagonal(D, np.inf)
    return float(np.mean(D.min(axis=1) < 0.1 * med))
